title: Northstar alignment compact - June checkpoint
body:
Purpose:
A short, portable checkpoint doc to align execs and org leads on a single northstar direction for the next 6 months, and to surface critical asks for the upcoming all-hands and exec update. This is intentionally compact — meant for review ahead of the alignment slot on 2025-06-18.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We propose adopting a single operational northstar for the company: 'sustained 99th-percentile tail latency under 150ms across hosted API regions while improving cost-per-1k-tokens by 15% versus baseline.' This couples performance (latency), reliability (tail), and economics (cost). Achieving it requires cross-org commitments across serving-runtime optimizations, Dedicated capacity policy changes, and product-level fallbacks.

Why a single northstar now:
- Removes noise: teams currently track multiple, sometimes conflicting metrics (median latency, total tokens, average cost).
- Forces tradeoffs: surface where teams must choose latency vs cost, and create clear escalation paths.
- Investor and customer signal: tangible SLO tied to our competitive positioning (production economics).

Proposed company-level OKRs (draft):
- OKR A: Production economics — make inference predictable and cheaper
  - KR A1: Reduce cost-per-1k-tokens across hosted API by 15% (Q3 baseline).
  - KR A2: Maintain 99th percentile tail latency <= 150ms in 3 primary regions (NA/EU/APAC) for baseline 95% traffic.
  - KR A3: Ship automatic model-variant fallback with latency-aware routing to handle 100% of capacity anomalies within 30s.

- OKR B: Platform reliability and trust
  - KR B1: Roll out token-level tracing in Console for top 10 customers (by volume).
  - KR B2: Decrease P2/P1 incident mean time to mitigation by 25% via playbooks and SRE runbooks.

- OKR C: Customer velocity and adoption (PLG + sales motions)
  - KR C1: Launch Dedicated onboarding templates for top 3 enterprise verticals and reduce time-to-first-QPS by 40%.
  - KR C2: Ship 5 reference apps demonstrating cost/latency tradeoffs (docs + tutorials).

Cross-org asks (what we need from execs / leads):
- Eng-serving-runtime: prioritize kernel selection and a short project to reduce KV cache cold-start for chat sessions. Estimate: 6 weeks, 2 FTE.
- Product-hosted-api: allow one-week feature flag window to test variant routing in prod with rollback paths. Need approval for controlled customer cohort.
- Dedicated & Sales: commit to one pilot enterprise customer for canary Dedicated autoscaling policy testing; marketing to prep a case study.
- SRE/Infra: allocate on-call rotation overlap for the first two weeks of rollout and prepare a mandatory postmortem template for fallback activation events.

All-hands (15-minute alignment slot) run-of-show suggestion:
- 0:00–2:00 — Context and the ask (Avery)
- 2:00–6:00 — Short explainer of the northstar and why it matters (VP Eng)
- 6:00–10:00 — Quick demo of the Console metric mockups (Product lead)
- 10:00–13:00 — Exec asks and commitments (Head of SRE, Head of Sales)
- 13:00–15:00 — Q&A and 3 immediate next steps + who owns them.

Decision record (explicit asks for this meeting):
- Approve northstar framing (latency tail + cost) — binary decision.
- Commit to the three company-level OKRs above as the operating set for the next cycle.
- Approve a small pilot (up to 2% of hosted traffic) for latency-aware routing with a 72-hour rollback SLA.

Risks & mitigations (short bullets):
- Risk: Northstar over-emphasizes latency and forces harmful model downgrades impacting quality.
  - Mitigation: Tie OKR A to a quality guardrail (weekly sample evals + user-facing NPS for affected customers).
- Risk: Engineering bandwidth — competing runway for Dedicated legal/compliance work.
  - Mitigation: Re-prioritize one mid-Q sprint and expand contractor budget for compliance tasks.
- Risk: Customers misinterpret pilot as general availability.
  - Mitigation: Clear marketing language, in-product banners for pilot cohorts, and targeted CS outreach.

Open questions / notes to resolve before exec sync:
- Should the northstar be a single scalar (latency threshold) or compound (latency + cost index)? Proposal recommends scalar for clarity but include cost KRs.
- Which exact traffic bucket(s) qualify for the 95% traffic baseline? Suggest: all single-tenant production traffic across hosted API.
- Org resource ask: confirm 2 FTE for KV cold-start work or propose alternatives (contractor, shifted scope).

Immediate next steps (owners + dates):
- By 2025-06-09 — Exec pre-read distributed (Avery).
- By 2025-06-13 — Runbook draft for fallback activation ready (Head SRE, Diego Ramos).
- By 2025-06-18 — Final decision in exec sync; if approved, announce northstar in all-hands (Avery + Comms).

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This doc is intentionally short; detailed playbooks, eval sets, and dashboards will be separate artifacts linked above.
- Please flag any missing stakeholder commitments inline in the Confluence thread or reply in #exec-sync-threads.

Appendix (links & sketches):
